factoryDeclaration.headerRewritten: The basis is now A-220's ruling and P-327's new-retirements-only rule: the 0.4694 that set 0.5 no longer enters the share at all (Williamson's 282,569 rows are re-retirements now, and the census reads zero NEW retirements in all six counties), so 0.05 refuses nothing measured as healthy. The header states plainly what 0.05 now refuses that 0.5 let through (the 5-to-50-percent band, i.e. a mass false retirement such as a 40-percent county loss, on the writer that emptied Bastrop) and what a legitimately large retirement must do (go through the existing population-bound authorisation, DESTRUCTIVE_WRITE_AUTHORISATION).

factoryWriters.sixFourThroughTheRealCallPath: test/destructive-write-guard.test.mjs G6 (violation): a 6 percent share REFUSES through requireRetirementGate -- the real publish call path, not a unit of assertBlastRadius alone; G6: a 4 percent share PROMOTES through the same call path and reports the share it took; G6: the same call path still refuses the Bastrop share (0.925) and names the token it would need.

unwiredReReadAt005.why: two hand-named place_keys re-verified live before the delete, already gated by an explicit AUTHORIZATION constant: a share is the wrong instrument, not a small one. 2 rows is 2 rows at 0.5, at 0.05 and at any number; a future set-valued mode is narrower in practice now (6 percent would refuse where 0.5 let it through).
one colliding pair at a time; no population to take a share of, so the number never enters the decision.
one colliding key at a time, deletes companion rows only -- neither half of the reason is size-dependent.
delete-and-reinsert is one rail's refresh bound by that source's own row count and its job's coverage check; a companion-rail refresh is not a destructive status and no threshold makes it refuse.

the closest group to the hazard: they reset a rail's own cells on the rows the rail no longer covers, a share near 1.0 on the normal path for a first full acquisition. Wiring them at 0.05 would refuse the ordinary run -- a permanently-red gate -- so they stay unwired and carry the escalation clause.

writes VALUES onto rows that stay live, never a status; the write happens in a bake subprocess, so a threshold here would refuse the wrong thing. Escalation clause stands: the day the bake writes a status, the invocation is gated on the rows it will touch.

factoryCrossRepoCheck.whatItCompares: the share, the authorisation variable name, the refusal codes, the token grammar and the factory content identity (git blob sha + bytes + sha256) -- the factory's own declaration against the engine's copy
factoryCrossRepoCheck.selftestFirst: `node scripts/check-engine-destructive-write-declaration.mjs --selftest` -> all 8 selftest fixtures pass: a copy still reading 0.5 is refused; an absent declaration is refused, not skipped; a renamed refusal code is refused; a pin whose factory content hash is stale is refused; a correct copy passes (not vacuous); a declaration on engine main WINS and the fallback is not consulted; an empty engine main reads the declared fallback and the note NAMES the ref it read; an empty engine main AND an empty fallback still REFUSE (absence is never a pass).
factoryCrossRepoCheck.mergeWindowFallback: The job checks out engine `main` and, only when main carries no declaration file, reads the engine's lane ref -- printing which ref it read ('read at <path> (engine main)' vs the declared fallback). It is a declared read of a named ref with every leg still compared, NOT a skip: absence at both refs refuses with its own code (ENGINE_DECLARATION_UNREADABLE).

engineDeclaration.headerRewritten: states that the direction of the change is the OPPOSITE of P-328's: the engine is unchanged (its writers have refused above 0.05 since P-213/P-275) and the factory tightened to meet it; the 5-to-50-percent loosening is gone.

pin.whyContentAddressed: This program squash-merges; a squash REPLACES the commit sha and leaves the blob untouched, so a commit-addressed pin would break the day the factory PR lands for a change that did not touch a byte of the pinned file -- a gate that fails for a reason unrelated to its subject (DEV_PROCESS's dead gate). Identity = blob sha + bytes + sha256, all three compared; `ref` is provenance only, and the check falls back to the clone's origin/main/main/HEAD, refusing only on a content mismatch or an unreadable factory. So it survives the branch being squashed and deleted.
